data.name: Balindar
data.gender_notes: Balindar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Balindar is derived from the Sanskrit words 'bal' (strength) and 'indra' (lord of thunder). This name is given to boys who are believed to possess the courage and might of Indra, the king of gods in Hindu mythology. The name Balindar carries the meaning “Brave in battle” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Balindar usually hope their child will grow to embody brave in battle and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Balindar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Brave in battle.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Balindar total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.reference: Balindar was a famous Brahmin king in ancient India, who ruled over the region of Vidarbha in the 6th century AD. He was a powerful ruler and was known for his wisdom and justice. Balindar is mentioned in several ancient Indian texts, including the Mahabharata and the Puranas.

historical_references.reference: Balindar is also known as Balin in the Hindu epic Ramayana. He was a friend and advisor to King Dasaratha, the father of Lord Rama. Balindar played a significant role in helping Dasaratha make important decisions during his reign, and was revered for his knowledge and understanding of the scriptures.
